Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-19 14:30 PST
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Priya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Marta (Procurement), Devon (Security), Samir (Legal), Olivia (Platform), Jordan (Finance)

Summary: Quick procurement + security gating sync to align MSA/DPA redlines, KMS/SSO integration notes, and pricing approval pathway. Customer flagged two blockers: (1) KMS key policies / HSM requirement for PHI-like workloads; (2) pricing approver wants committed vs consumption model comparison.

Topics: MSA redlines, DPA data residency clause, SLA targets and uptime credits, KMS/HSM integration options, SSO/SAML provisioning, pricing approval workflow and PO timing, pilot scope + technical checklist.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Priya: hey everyone, thanks for coming on, i think we scheduled 45 but we have 46 on the calendar uh so we'll run through the ask which is legal + procurement integration, right, pricing and kms handoff. i'll quick intro, i'm priya kapoor, enterprise AE for Redwood, and with me is ethan morales, our systems eng focused on private deployments and key management.
[00:18] Marta: hi all, marta ruiz here, head of procurement for aurelia, quick note, we have Samir from legal and Devon from sec cause this is mostly security gating. thanks for making time.
[00:26] Ethan: morning, yeah, hi, good to meet, Olivia and Jordan as well?
[00:30] Olivia: hey, i'm olivia, platform eng, i'll be on the pilot.
[00:33] Jordan: jordan in finance, quick background, we own PO timing and approvals.
[00:36] Samir: samir, counsel. we'll be level-setting on the dpa and msa.

[01:00] Priya: great. quick agenda: 1) where procurement and legal are on the MSA/DPA redlines, 2) KMS and HSM requirements and our private offering, 3) pricing approval path, committed vs consumption, and 4) pilot kickoff next steps. does that look right?
[01:10] Marta: yes. we also want to confirm SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning for user orgs; that's a gating item.

[01:22] Ethan: absolutely, we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning in our console for enterprise, and for private deployments we can integrate with on-prem SSO as well. note, sometimes the naming in exports is weird in the console but operationally it's standard SAML flows.
[01:35] Devon: thanks. primary security asks from my side: 1) KMS key control - we need customer-owned keys; 2) audit logs retention and immutable audit for 365 days; 3) data residency - certain payloads must stay in eu-west-1. can you confirm those map to your private deployment?
[01:53] Ethan: yes, for private we provide customer-managed KMS integration; you can configure the key in your cloud KMS and we call encrypt/decrypt using that. for on-prem HSM we also have an integration path, it requires a short runbook and our SE team to sit on the connection. about audit logs, we can push logs to your splunk or cloud logging endpoint and set retention, but the immutable audit piece may depend on your logging tier - we can discuss append-only storage or an escrow for compliance.
[02:14] Samir: on the MSA+DPA, our legal redlines include stronger breach notification timelines (24 hours), tighter subprocessors list, and an explicit prohibition of model training on customer data. we've seen vague language in other vendors and want explicit clause.
[02:30] Priya: understood. we recently updated our DPA to include a non-training clause but i'll get the exact paragraph in the redline. i'll share the updated MSA/DPA with tracked changes.
[02:38] Samir: also SLA language - we typically ask for 99.95 for core endpoints and credits tied to response latencies. is that something you can commit to?
[02:45] Ethan: our hosted tier has public SLA tiers, for dedicated/reserved we can negotiate 99.95 with financial credits; the private deployment SLA depends on network/ops responsibilities. often customers retain some responsibility for infra uptime in private models. we can draft an SLA that accounts for shared-responsibility.
[03:03] Jordan: from finance perspective, we need to compare committed reserved capacity (discounted) vs consumption-based. if we commit to 6-12 month reserved capacity what discount bands are there and are there overage terms?
[03:16] Priya: good question. we've got standard reserved tiers: 20% for 6-mo, 30% for 12-mo on token spend for dedicated GPU pools; we can provide a blended unit cost spreadsheet. overage typically bills at a higher per-token than committed— we can show examples at 100k tokens/day. i'll attach the finance worksheet.
[03:31] Jordan: can you also show a scenario where we start with hosted, then move to dedicated once we hit usage thresholds? we need migration costs included.
[03:40] Ethan: yes, migration is mostly config and model pinning, the biggest cost is data transfer and any egress; we have migration runbook and can do a dry run in a sandbox. there may be a brief cutoff for cache warming but no data loss.
[03:53] Devon: back to KMS: we need a Customer Managed Key (CMK) with HSM-backed protection and key rotation controls. does Redwood support BYOK with HSM requirement? we've seen vendors say yes but only with hosted black box.
[04:05] Ethan: we support BYOK for both cloud KMS (e.g., AWS KMS) with HSM and on-prem HSM through a direct connector. HSM-level attestations are possible but we need to confirm FIPS/HSM model compatibility. if you send the HSM make/model and key policy we'll validate.
[04:18] Samir: also, we need to understand where keys are stored: redwood-managed KMS vs customer KMS. the MSA needs clarity on key custody and what happens on termination.
[04:26] Priya: we'll add specific custody language to the MSA: customer retains key ownership; Redwood only has transient access to decrypt at runtime for private deployment; upon contract termination we'll provide a verified key revocation and data purge statement. i'll draft suggested language.
[04:39] Olivia: from a platform perspective the engineering ask is around network egress and VPC peering. we want to know the port ranges and whether there are any persistent tunnels.
[04:48] Ethan: for private we use a short-lived TLS tunnel and optionally a VPC endpoint/peering depending on cloud. port 443 only for control; for direct host-level traffic we use configured subnets, we'll provide exact CIDR ranges and netflow diagrams. i'll send the topology.
[05:02] Marta: procurement process — we need the MSA/DPA in final redline, pricing sheet, and a statement of work for the pilot. decision committee meets on 1/28 and procurement needs everything 3 business days prior. can you commit to 1/22 for docs?
[05:16] Priya: yes, we can aim for 1/22 to get you redlines and pricing. ethan will send technical docs by 1/21.
[05:24] Samir: one more legal note: we have an escrow requirement and a clause around export controls (we operate in EU and US). any issues?
[05:33] Priya: export control clauses are standard; we have a DPA variant for EU data residency. for escrow we can discuss a third-party escrow provider and include an SLA for code escrow if required.
[05:41] Jordan: for approvals: who at redwood signs the MSA? we need to know the signature authority level and if the invoice addresses are on the MSA.
[05:49] Priya: Redwood legal will sign with our standard signatories; i'll include our billing entity and remittance details in the MSA.
[05:55] Devon: one more thing — incident response: we want a 24x7 SOC contact and runbook for breach notification tied to the 24-hour contractual window. redwood has SOC capabilities?
[06:05] Ethan: we don't provide SOC-as-a-service but we have on-call incident response for enterprise customers, with a pager rotation and SLAs for initial ack. we can publish the contact and runbook and include it as an appendix.
[06:18] Samir: great. quick check — any competitors in your shortlist? we've done RFPs with LambdaServe and MajorCloud AI; they have similar features but we've seen differing MSA exceptions.
[06:29] Priya: understood; we'll provide references and a comparison doc if helpful. our differentiation is private KMS/quantization profiles and predictable dedicated latency.
[06:38] Marta: timeline: procurement committee meets 1/28, legal needs final MSA by 1/24 to review. pricing approver needs a PO request by 1/29. are we aligned?
[06:45] Priya: aligned — we will hit 1/22 for redlines and pricing, gives you buffer.

[07:00] Recap: Priya to send MSA/DPA redline + pricing sheet; Ethan to send topology, KMS/HSM compatibility checklist, and pilot SOW draft; Customer to confirm approver path and PO date.

[07:15] Closing: thanks all. we'll put the action items in CRM and schedule a pilot kickoff for week of 1/26 if procurement clears.
